clue.text: Deny one plugs hit record at first

indicators.note: tells us the record comes at the front, ahead of the rest of the word
the one fills a gap in the word for hit, as a plug fills a hole

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat

explanation.surface: Someone denies that a vinyl single was ever a hit, or that one song made it big first.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim something is to renounce or refuse responsibility for it, a formal way of denying it.

clue.text: Blue movie of Hitchcock's right to go after terror

indicators.note: the film and the right come after the terror in the answer

parts.note: a little terror is a mischievous child, an imp

explanation.surface: A smutty film by Hitchcock about the right to follow terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of risqué or smutty is close to improper, indecent.

clue.text: Bells ring only up to noon during visit

indicators.note: the shortened ring goes inside the word for visit

parts.note: to call on is to visit

indicators.note: only the letters before N (noon) are kept, so the word stops short

explanation.surface: Church bells ring only until midday during someone's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: N for noon is a standard abbreviation; ring is cut off just before its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned bells played from a keyboard.

clue.text: Truant's old boring tool cases

definitions.note: read as 'Truant is', so the definition is an adjective describing the truant

indicators.note: the boring tool encloses the letter for old, like a case

explanation.surface: A truant's old drill comes in cases.
explanation.definitionFit: AWOL, absent without leave, describes someone missing without permission, as a truant is.

clue.text: In Paris, my sister picked up a rubber

indicators.note: heard, so the French phrase is replaced by a word that sounds like it

explanation.surface: In Paris, someone's sister brought home an eraser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' looks like an eraser; it is someone who rubs, a massage therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur gives massages, literally one who rubs the body.

clue.text: Cryptic indication of Sally or Jack's rank

wordplay.note: Sally splits as S (second) plus ALLY (mate), so the answer phrase is a cryptic clue to that name

explanation.surface: A clue for a woman's name, or a sailor's position.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay gives S + ALLY. A jack, or jack tar, is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Second mate is an officer rank on a merchant ship, below the first mate.

clue.text: Favourable result — reverse of home leg in capital city

indicators.note: the word for home is written back to front

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
peg is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: A team wins after a home-and-away tie in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnipeg is the capital of the Canadian province of Manitoba.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnipeg is a provincial capital city in Canada.

clue.text: United fans excited by rising score in tie? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: worked up, so the letters of fans are stirred around
in a down entry, going up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to net is to score a goal

explanation.surface: United supporters get carried away when their side scores to win a cup tie.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of tie, i.e. untie.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten is to undo or release, the reverse of tying something.

clue.text: Hostility from states no one's backing

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: going backwards, so the two short words here are read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone declares that nobody supports a hostile stance.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or antipathy, close in sense to hostility.

clue.text: Fake sign of unpaid bill in English club

indicators.note: the bill sign sits inside the club's name

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club
an IOU ('I owe you') is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A dodgy IOU turns up at an English football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the everyday name of Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means false or not genuine, a ready synonym for fake.

clue.text: Untidy person content to leave India for European country

parts.note: a sloven is someone careless about appearance

indicators.note: the inner letters of India go away, leaving only its outside

explanation.surface: A slob is happy to quit India and move to Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' here is the noun, what is contained, not the adjective meaning happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a nation in central Europe, bordering Italy and Austria.

clue.text: Charmed in brief period before spring

indicators.note: the brief period comes ahead of the spring in the answer

parts.note: a spell is a short stretch of time
to bound is to leap or spring

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted by a short spell ahead of the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season but is the verb meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound means enthralled, as if held by a magic charm.

clue.text: When one may get a nasty shock?

definitions.text: When one may get a nasty
definitions.meaning: the surface suggests a frightening moment or event
a shock of hair, a thick mass of it

explanation.walkthrough: A shock is also a mass of hair, so a nasty shock is unruly hair, not a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad hair day is a day when one's hair looks unmanageable, and generally a day when things go wrong.

clue.text: Returned garments displaying blemish

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for the garments is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Clothes sent back to the shop show a flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small mark or stain, a kind of blemish.

clue.text: Cordial but not popular? One may blow up

indicators.note: the word for popular is dropped from the cordial

parts.note: grenadine is a sweet pomegranate syrup

explanation.surface: A soft drink that isn't well liked might still go off with a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb that explodes, so it is a thing that may blow up.

clue.text: Showing appreciation of a quantity of ashes?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as '...', as much as a fire grate holds, like spoonful

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a whimsical coinage: the amount of ash a grate can hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Grateful means feeling or expressing thanks, and a grate full of ashes is the punning reading.

clue.text: The very bright edges of earring and garish extra decorations

indicators.note: only the outside letters of each following word are used

explanation.surface: Flashy jewellery and extra trimmings around the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads are intellectuals, people considered highly clever.

clue.text: Executive's helper to keep teasing model

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant
to rag on someone is to tease them persistently

explanation.surface: A boss's assistant must go on mocking a model.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Account sort code with money staked externally

indicators.note: the stake goes around the outside of the rearranged code

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so the letters of code are reordered

explanation.surface: A bank account's sort code, with money deposited outside it.
explanation.walkthrough: A sort code is the British number identifying a bank branch.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short account of an incident, a story.

clue.text: Soldiers take steps to secure new weaponry

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the dance holds the letter for new inside it

parts.note: to dance is to step to music

explanation.surface: Troops act to obtain fresh weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take steps' sounds like taking action; it is dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means military weapons and ammunition, especially artillery.

clue.text: How amazing to be welcomed by host one meets

indicators.note: the answer is taken in by the words that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of host, all of one, and the start of meets

explanation.surface: A guest is astonished by the warm reception a host gives everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone me is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'well I never'.

clue.text: Ship moving slowly out of lake

indicators.note: the lake's letter is taken out of the musical term

parts.note: largo is a musical direction for a slow tempo

explanation.surface: A ship crawls out of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the legendary vessel of Jason and his Argonauts.

clue.text: Ancient disheartened by present day possibly is prepared

indicators.note: with its heart gone, only the first and last letters of ancient stay

parts.note: to be present is to be there

indicators.note: the letters of day might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something old, gloomy at modern times, is nonetheless ready for action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' reads as sad but means the middle of the word is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: At the ready means poised for immediate use, in a state of preparation.

clue.text: Something elementary in Reagan campaign slogan?

wordplay.note: Ronald Reagan's first name shortens to Ron, and a campaign slogan urges voters to choose him in an election

explanation.surface: A question about a basic idea in a presidential campaign slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ELECT RON, a call to vote for Ronald Reagan.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron is a subatomic particle, and 'elementary' hints at elementary particles of physics.

clue.text: Unemployed compiler given hand-out, short of nothing

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: lacking, so the round letter for nothing is removed

explanation.surface: A jobless setter on benefits gets nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the British term for state unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean out of work, without a job.

clue.text: Tail pinned to cuckoo

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tail fixed onto a cuckoo, like a party game.
explanation.definitionFit: An end point is the final part of something, the tail end.

clue.text: How one may serve in Germany and with marines after a long time

indicators.note: the marines come after the long time in the answer

parts.note: an era is a long period

explanation.surface: Someone might do military service in Germany and with the marines after many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' suggests military service, but it is the tennis or cricket sense: an underarm delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Underarm describes a delivery with the hand below shoulder height, a way to serve the ball.

clue.text: Explanations of say French art welcomed by lovers once

indicators.note: the former partners take in the other pieces between them

parts.note: es is French for 'art', as in 'thou art'

explanation.surface: Former lovers explain an example of French art they welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the archaic verb (thou art), whose French equivalent is es (tu es).
explanation.definitionFit: Exegeses are critical interpretations, especially of scripture, so they are explanations.
